correctness.rationale: The theorem is reconstructed by a rank-k projector with diagonal k/n and edge quadratic form k mu/m, yielding an exact Rayleigh budget bound for every independent conductance assignment. Uniform rates attain it by the explicit two-by-two spectral branches. Equality forces every pendant rate, and monotonicity of the branch identifies precisely the optimal base-rate face. Complex Fourier and complete-graph Fiedler-space arguments prove unrestricted uniqueness in the stated families. All boundary cases n>=3,t>0,B>0 are covered. Standalone tests passed 4209 finite assertions; tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The closed form handles every vertex-and-edge-transitive connected base, including cycles, cliques, hypercubes, Petersen and balanced bicliques, with independent edge allocation. A nontrivial equality argument exactly transfers the entire optimal face and proves all pendant rates fixed, distinguishing guaranteed rigidity from potentially nonunique base designs. The result gives an analytical speed/budget law and split depending only on graph invariants n,m,mu, avoiding graph-specific semidefinite solves; it is a motivated network diffusion design result, not an arbitrary finite table.
